name: Speak Easy Virtual Call Center (Office or Home)
desc:
Customer Success Representative (Attorney Accounts) | $20-$22/hr | Inbound/Outbound, No Sales Expectations
Company: Speak Easy Marketing Inc.
Industry: Legal Marketing Services
What Your Day Will Look Like:
This one's worth explaining carefully since the title sounds sales-y but the posting is explicit that it isn't. You'd be the main point of contact for a set group of attorney clients (criminal defense, DUI, personal injury, divorce, and bankruptcy lawyers), helping them get the most out of the marketing services they're already paying for. Think account manager, not salesperson. You'd onboard new clients, walk them through setup like Google Maps and social media access, check in regularly by phone and email, review how their marketing results are trending, and flag anything that needs escalating to another team. A big part of the job is just staying organized and keeping every client relationship on track, so this is equal parts relationship building and quiet behind the scenes admin work.
assessment: Not explicitly named, but there is a real screening step. Applicants apply by email with a specific subject line, a written explanation of fit, their time zone, a resume, and a short recorded audio sample reading aloud from an article so the company can hear the applicant's speaking voice.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: Not stated in posting.
Required Experience: Not stated by years. A strong track record of success and self-discipline working from home are called out as real qualifiers.
Preferred Experience: Familiarity with Zoom Phone and Zoho, though not required.
Required Skills:
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, Gmail, and Google Drive
Strong written and verbal communication
Ability to manage deadlines and stay organized
Self-motivated and proactive, comfortable bringing ideas forward rather than just following instructions
Coachable and open to direction
Best Fit
 This role is ideal for:
Someone with strong organizational habits who can manage multiple client relationships and deadlines without close supervision
Someone genuinely comfortable working with attorneys and clients going through difficult legal situations (DUI, divorce, bankruptcy, criminal defense, personal injury)
Someone who wants real earning growth over time through pay increases, renewal bonuses, and review bonuses
Someone self-disciplined enough to stay productive working from home with real freedom in their schedule
Not a Good Fit for:
Anyone who dislikes lawyers or is uncomfortable with the idea that these clients serve people in difficult legal situations, since the posting is explicit that this isn't the right fit for that mindset
Anyone who needs a fully scripted, closely supervised role, since this requires real independent judgment and follow-through
Anyone not comfortable submitting a recorded voice sample as part of applying
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
Client account management
Customer success
Legal marketing
Client onboarding
Relationship retention
Microsoft Excel and Google Drive
Written and verbal communication
Deadline management
Independent contractor
Attorney client services
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
 This one does not follow the standard 4 step process. Applicants respond directly by email to opportunities@speakeasymarketinginc.com with the exact subject line "Customer Success Representative for Attorneys, [Your State]." The email must include why the applicant is a good fit, their time zone, a resume, and a short recorded audio clip reading the first 5 sentences of any online article aloud, so the company can hear the applicant's speaking voice. Applications that don't follow the subject line instructions are disregarded. Total time to hire is not stated.
4-5 things to be ready to speak to in the application email:
Why do you feel you'd be a great fit for this role specifically?
What is your time zone, and does it fit the 9 AM to 5 PM Central availability window?
How do you stay organized managing multiple client relationships and deadlines at once?
How do you feel about working closely with attorneys and clients in difficult legal situations like divorce or criminal defense?
What does being self-disciplined and productive while working from home look like for you day to day?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
Pay: Starting at $20/hr, paid weekly via ACH, increasing to $22/hr after a 90 day performance review. After 6 months, eligible for a "book of business" bonus based on a percentage of monthly payments from managed clients. Additional bonus opportunities include 15% commission on upsells, $500 or more per contract renewal, and $100 for each verified Google review from a client.
Shift: At least 20 hours per week, Monday through Friday, between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM Central. Hours can grow over time.
Benefits: Not stated in posting. This is a 1099 independent contractor role, so no employer-provided benefits should be assumed unless confirmed directly.
Equipment Provided: Not provided. Participant needs their own computer, phone, reliable internet, and a quiet workspace.
Felony Friendly?: Not stated in posting.
Drug Test: Not stated in posting.
Notes: This is a genuinely interesting one because the earning potential grows meaningfully over time (pay increase at 90 days, book of business bonus at 6 months, plus multiple bonus types), which is a stronger long-term earning structure than most 1099 roles in this database. The voice recording requirement in the application is unusual, so prepare a participant for that ahead of time so it doesn't catch them off guard. This role genuinely requires comfort working with attorneys serving people in hard legal situations, so it's worth having an honest conversation with a participant about whether that sits well with them before they apply.
Career Pathway: Not stated directly in posting. Based on the role's structure, a reasonable path would be Customer Success Representative → Senior Client Success Manager → Client Success Team Lead → Director of Client Services, though this is an estimate, not confirmed by the company.
training: discussed in interview/ofer stage. must be available for any shift
